A classical effect of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) is demonstrated in a planar metamaterials in the ultraviolet regime.
The EIT unit cell consists of a vertical cut wire as the bright resonator and two horizontal cut wire pairs as the dark element.
The frequency absorption band of the ultra-broadband infrared absorber has a FWHM of 86% at normal incidence, the largest bandwidth reported.
The plasmonic super absorber etched on a gold film can provide broadband and polarization-independent resonant light absorption over the entire visible spectrum with an averaged absorption above 90%.
An arbitrarily thin metamaterial layer with real parts of permittivity and permeability equal to zero can perfectly absorb or giantly amplify an incident plane wave at a critical angle.
Metamaterial absorbers are combined with amorphous silicon to create terahertz modulators where the reflected wave amplitude can be strongly modulated.
The planar EIT metamaterial structure can be easily fabricated and integrated as an ultra-compact sensor with high sensitivity.
The broadband slow-wave absorbers can be utilized in photovoltaic devices, thermal emitters, and high-responsivity broadband detectors.
An extremely sub-wavelength planar magnetic metamaterial made up of periodic dual layer spirals is demonstrated in the terahertz regime.
Five journal publications resulting from this AOARD-funded project are listed, including articles in high-impact journals such as Nano Letters.
